safety.title: Job and employment scams - Competition Bureau Canada
safety.notes: Official Bureau tips page (search result; not opened). Warns about guaranteed high income for little effort, upfront fees for business plans/start-up kits/software, using your bank account to pass payments, and fake-cheque overpayment schemes.
tips: Be suspicious of jobs that guarantee high income for little effort
Never pay upfront for a 'business plan', start-up kit or software to get work
No legitimate business sends you a cheque and asks you to transfer part back
Research offers independently and get advice before agreeing
Do not give banking or card details to people you do not know and trust

safety.title: Job Search Safety Tips - Job Bank
safety.notes: Official Job Bank safety page (search result; not opened). Advice on protecting personal information, reporting suspicious postings and immigration-related email scams.
tips: Legitimate employers will not ask for banking information to apply
Keep your SIN, birth date and licence or health card numbers off your resume and out of early interviews
Use 'Report a problem with this job posting' on Job Bank if something looks wrong
Job Bank does not handle immigration; distrust emails offering immigration services in its name
Look for the 'Posted on Job Bank' flag on postings created by registered employers

safety.title: O. Reg. 99/23: Licensing - Temporary Help Agencies and Recruiters, Employment Standards Act, 2000
safety.notes: Ontario regulation requiring temp help agencies and recruiters to be licensed (search result; not opened). Fee prohibition for workers reported by secondary sources (Parkdale Community Legal Services, Canadian HR Reporter), not confirmed on an ontario.ca guide page.
tips: In Ontario, temp help agencies and recruiters must hold a licence
Ontario temp agencies may not charge workers a fee to be hired or assigned work (per legal-clinic and HR press reports)
